Bessent emphasized that ultimate authority over placing foreign firms on the U.S. Entity List rests with the Commerce Department, despite repeated warnings from Treasury and intelligence officials regarding Megaspeed's alleged circumvention of U.S. export controls.

Scrutiny over the enforcement delay has intensified following revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of acting as a Chinese intelligence operative involved in routing $7.5 billion worth of restricted AI chips to China.

The Commerce Department denied reports of the heated Situation Room clash, maintaining that Entity List designations are made collectively at the administration level rather than unilaterally by Commerce, even as White House advisers reportedly discuss Lutnick's potential ouster.
title: Bessent Says Lutnick’s Commerce Department Is Responsible for Failure to Blacklist Megaspeed

Lambert, who owned a penthouse in the Metropole Condominiums, had been in active litigation since 2025 against the Metropole Condominium Association over alleged water and mold damage to his unit.

Before the shooting, Lambert documented grievances on an X account called OfMiceandMold, posting engineering reports and photos. He later barricaded himself in his seventh-floor apartment, dying of a self-inflicted gunshot after police negotiations.

Metropolitan Police Department Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll confirmed authorities recovered three firearms from the apartment. Nearby schools lifted lockdowns by 11:30 a.m. as investigators examined the connection between the shooting and the condo dispute.

Council Member Brooke Pinto described the tragedy as 'senseless,' as officials investigate whether the attack was targeted. The incident occurred amid 479 mass shootings nationwide in 2026, according to the Mass Shooting Tracker.
title: Washington DC Shooter Identified as Dr Matt Lambert After Gym Gunfire Leaves One Dead and Four Injured

Allegations involved Alice Huang, suspected of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice-president of health care. After Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter confronted Huang, he confessed, prompting the board to investigate.

Huang's hands-on management of around 60 executives deteriorated significantly as the scandal unfolded. According to people who spoke with him, he surrendered his usual demeanor, using phrases such as "whatever" and "I don't care" while castigating himself as a "piece of s***".

Interim CEO Colette Kress pledged to reassure employees, scheduling an all-hands meeting for November 18. A day earlier, Nvidia reports quarterly results that Wall Street analysts predict will show a near doubling of sales growth.

In the coming weeks, Huang is expected to testify before Congress regarding his relationship with Alice Huang. Politicians will question whether the association potentially put secrets of Nvidia's state-of-the-art chips at risk.
title: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had relationship with second employee: Reuters

summary: On Thursday, Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately as president, CEO and board member, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones appointed as the company's first-ever board chairman.

Revelations of two extramarital affairs—one with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of Chinese espionage, and another with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia vice president—intensified pressure on the CEO.
Nvidia shares plummeted more than 10% in premarket trading Thursday, erasing more than $600 billion in market value during the week as investors reacted to the leadership vacuum.

Nvidia's board launched a search for a permanent successor considering internal and external candidates, while confirming third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings will release as scheduled Tuesday, November 17.

Market intelligence firm Morningstar warned that Huang's exit could lead to less AI dealmaking and greater regulation, threatening the stability of the ecosystem he helped bankroll through Nvidia's infrastructure investments.
title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO Amid Independent Probe Into Security and Conduct

summary: On Wednesday, Nov. 11, Democrat Scott Colom, a district attorney, defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith , becoming Mississippi's first Black United States senator since Reconstruction and giving Democrats at least 55 Senate seats.

Hyde-Smith blocked Colom's 2022 nomination to a federal judgeship using the blue slip privilege, a political maneuver that backfired and prompted the district attorney to challenge her for the Senate seat instead.
Focusing on pocketbook issues, Colom flipped several Republican counties and gained momentum with viral ads that mocked Hyde-Smith’s suggestion to "pick another protein."

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and DSCC Chair Senator Kirsten Gillibrand called the victory historic, vowing to partner with Colom "to fight for Mississippians' health care, costs, and future."

Nearly 99 percent of ballots have been processed, according to the Associated Press, and Colom is set to be sworn in early next year, marking a significant shift in the Deep South’s political landscape.
title: Scott Colom Flips Mississippi Senate Seat After Weeklong Provisional Ballot Review

Jensen Huang resigned after reports of a relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang, whom authorities suspect of spying for China, while lawmakers criticized Lutnick for refusing to blacklist Chinese companies.

Donors aligned with Vance, known as the Rockbridge Network, met in Houston this week to regroup while awaiting his decision. Terry Schilling, president of the American Principles Project, said, "I would be surprised if he doesn't run.
title: JD Vance Is Considering Not Running for President in 2028: CNN

The arrest occurs three years after Wolgamott pleaded guilty to a previous DWI in Kanabec County, where he was caught driving with a blood alcohol level above 0.09.

title: Minnesota Rep. Dan Wolgamott arrested on suspicion of DWI

The Iran war and resulting energy supply shock sent Fuel prices markedly higher in recent months, though growth slowed compared to September's 1.4% rate.
Wholesale inflation stood at 3.1% a year ago, meaning prices remain well above the Federal Reserve 's 2% annual target set by policymakers.
Stubbornly high prices soured Americans on the economy, fueling significant Democratic gains in midterm elections last week.
Although the PPI does not translate directly to the Consumer Price Index, its trajectory and category-specific price hikes serve as a potential bellwether for consumer costs ahead.
title: Wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, putting annual rate at 6.5%, the highest in nearly four years

At the UP Summit in Florida on Thursday, SpaceX Vice President of Launch Kiko Dontchev revealed the flight date, according to Ars Technica's Eric Berger who attended.
Elon Musk has described Starship Flight 15 as a "profound technology milestone" in rocket science, with the mission aiming to catch both stages using the tower's mechanical arms.
The FAA's Starship page does not yet list a Flight 15 license, though SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell expects approval to cover a return to the launch site.
SpaceX aims to have Starship fully operational before the Artemis III mission, while Musk claimed in-orbit refueling missions "will be more like six to eight" rather than initial estimates.
title: SpaceX to attempt first Starship spacecraft recovery on land in 15th flight

summary: On Thursday, Judge John G. Koeltl sentenced Yuanjun Tang, 69, to three years' probation in Manhattan federal court after Tang admitted to spying on fellow activists for the Chinese government for five years.
Originally a 1989 Tiananmen Square protester, Tang defected to America in 2002 and confessed to providing information to the Ministry of State Security for about $4,200 annually.

Tang exploited his status to enable a handler to infiltrate a chat group with 140 Chinese-American individuals and recorded protests, including a 2023 Manhattan event dedicated to Tiananmen Square victims.
Four individuals who believe they were victimized spoke at sentencing. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jane Chong stated Tang's actions "had a chilling effect on an entire community of people."
Defense attorney Michael Bradley argued Tang sought to visit ailing parents, while Judge Koeltl noted that claims Tang targeted families for harm could not be proven.
title: Chinese dissident who admitted spying for Beijing in the US gets no jail time

British police, in cooperation with the American Army and the FBI, conducted a sting operation where Tyner unknowingly spoke with authorities regarding protected information.

Tyner, a veteran of Afghanistan, Iraq, and Qatar, reportedly failed to transfer any sensitive information to Moscow; officials confirmed the investigation remains active under Army Counterintelligence Command.
Authorities in Britain are expected to file an indictment against Tyner in the coming days, after which the United States intends to prosecute him under American military law.

Brigadier General Sean Stinchon, commanding general of Army Counterintelligence Command, called the case "a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent." Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied any connection.

summary: The Food and Drug Administration has effectively shelved the National Priority Voucher program, a fast-track drug review initiative launched by former Commissioner Marty Makary in June 2025.
Designed to compress review timelines to as little as one or two months, the program has stalled since the executive council of political appointees went dormant following Makary's departure in May.

Health policy professor Holly Fernandez Lynch at the University of Pennsylvania described the initiative as "the worst of both worlds," citing risks of political influence and potentially limited practical benefit.
While the agency continues accepting new voucher applications, sources indicate submissions are not advancing, with career scientists now resuming oversight of standard drug review timelines.
Leadership challenges, including the lack of a permanent commissioner, have contributed to the program's decline; no new vouchers have been issued since Makary departed.
title: US FDA shelves commissioner's voucher program for speedy drug reviews: Report

Microsoft Corp. determined that the elevated load stemmed from a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable, straining the remaining infrastructure rather than from increased traffic.
Queensland Health Services, supporting a 130,000 strong workforce, faced significant disruption, while Downdetector Australia recorded more than 4,400 reports of Outlook problems by 8:20am Friday.
ASIO Director-General Mike Burgess noted similarities to the 2024 CrowdStrike incident that crashed nearly 8.5 million computers, stating systems were affected "but not completely."
University of Melbourne Associate Professor Adel Toosi warned that reliance on major cloud providers creates systemic vulnerability, cautioning, "If all of them are failing, nothing can be done.
title: Microsoft outage continues as planned fixes are not working as expected, company says

Defense lawyers contend Owen testified to grand jurors that blood spatter was found on Murdaugh's T-shirt when no blood spatter was actually detected on his clothing.

Prosecutors argue "a single mistake is not bad faith" and maintain ample probable cause exists; Owen was also involved in a separate murder case dismissed last year for failing to disclose evidence to attorneys.

If Judge McCaslin grants the dismissal, prosecutors may seek new grand jury indictments as soon as next month; the retrial for murders of Maggie Murdaugh and Paul Murdaugh remains scheduled for April 5 next year in Sumter.

title: Alex Murdaugh wants murder indictments dismissed, saying agent lied to grand jury

Rains carry ash and organic matter into streams, where they react with chlorine to form "disinfection byproducts," which the Environmental Protection Agency regulates because they can cause illnesses, including cancer.

In Las Vegas, New Mexico, the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon wildfire contaminated the Gallinas River in 2022, forcing residents to rely on bottled water and shipments for years as local supplies remained unsafe.

State and federal governments allocated $148 million to rebuild the city's water treatment plant, with Las Vegas Mayor David Romero confirming that groundbreaking for the new facility is slated for Nov. 18.

Climate change and drought conditions have intensified the wildfire crisis, with 68,179 blazes burning more than 9.5 million acres so far in 2026, exacerbating long-term water quality threats across the nation.
title: Bigger and more-frequent wildfires threaten water supplies across the US

summary: On Thursday, President Lai Ching-te announced Taiwan is participating in the Asia -Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' summit in China on the principle of interaction on an "equal basis," after requesting written guarantees from Beijing.

China hosts the summit in Shenzhen next week amid tense relations, with Beijing refusing to speak with Lai and labeling him a "separatist" while conducting daily military operations around the island.

President Lai appointed Acer founder Stan Shih as his envoy to the summit. Taiwan typically selects business executives as envoys to avoid political complications while engaging with friendly delegations from the US and Japan.

Presidential office spokesperson Karen Kuo warned Taiwan will request immediate correction if unfair treatment occurs, stating "No member should use unilateral political conditions to interfere with or affect the terms of participation of other members."

China's foreign ministry stated on Wednesday it handles Taiwan's participation "in accordance with the one-China principle and the rules and customs of relevant APEC memorandums of understanding," allowing representatives to attend meetings "as normal.
title: Taiwan is taking part in APEC China summit on an 'equal basis,' president says

summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's U.S. Senate race on Wednesday, with The Associated Press calling the election after his lead extended to nearly 5,000 votes.

Colom, a 43-year-old local prosecutor, ran an underdog campaign capitalizing on electorate discontent with the economy. Last month, he engaged supporters waiting in 10 miles of lines at a rally held by President Donald Trump in Corinth, Mississippi.

On Thursday, Trump praised the senator-elect on Stephen A. Smith's "Straight Shooter" podcast, noting Colom's "chutzpah" for engaging voters. This contrasts sharply with Trump's earlier denigration of Colom as a "Marxist radical."

Colom will become Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since Civil War Reconstruction. Local officials confirmed the historic result after processing absentee and provisional ballots over several days.

The election outcome surprised observers, reflecting Colom's focus on economic issues like the Iran war and tariffs rather than personal attacks. His strategy successfully reached voters who traditionally back the Republican Party.
title: Trump praises Democrat Scott Colom for showing up to Mississippi rally and courting MAGA supporters

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Jeffries’s position as a reformist challenge, stressing that policy “needs to change,” congressional oversight of military aid, and scrutiny of “vehement pro-Israel” Democrats.

Right-Leaning coverage portrays the proposal as disruptive, using “demands,” “sweeping changes,” “major overhaul,” and an “unacceptable” status quo, while spotlighting his reluctance to oppose expanded defense cooperation.

Center coverage softens the divide by attributing “dramatic change,” noting his two-state support and criticism of Trump’s “reckless and costly war of choice.” All agree Jeffries seeks a major shift involving Israel and military policy, revealing tensions over security, diplomacy, party leadership, and America’s regional role.
summary: On Thursday, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries called for "dramatic change" in U.S. policy toward Israel, Gaza, and the West Bank, reaffirming support for a two-state solution at a press conference.

Jeffries' remarks followed a proposal by Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen and 11 other senators to remove the "U.S.-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative" from the National Defense Authorization Act.

While stopping short of endorsing the senators' proposal, Jeffries indicated the existing framework governing U.S. military assistance should be reconsidered; the Memorandum of Understanding provides $3.8 billion annually.

Democrats face internal pressure over military aid, as many members campaigned against it during recent midterm elections, placing party leadership under scrutiny as they prepare to take control of Congress.

The current Memorandum of Understanding expires in 2028, and Jeffries emphasized the status quo is "unacceptable," envisioning a secure Israel living side by side with an independent Palestinian state.
title: US House Democratic Leader Jeffries wants 'dramatic change' in Middle East

bias: Left-Leaning coverage foregrounds cross-party alignment, portraying Hawley as having “joined Dems” behind a nationwide “moratorium,” while right-leaning coverage stresses consumer protection from higher electric bills and political fallout, using “protect Americans,” “freeze,” and “shellacking.” The center emphasizes institutional significance—Hawley as the “highest-ranking” or “first” Republican supporter—and urgency before Republicans potentially lose their majority.
The pivotal divide is whether the proposal signifies bipartisan regulatory action, electoral repositioning, or household-cost relief.

Despite differing tones and implications, all perspectives highlight Hawley’s Republican identity and support for temporarily halting new data-center construction, reflecting broader disputes over regulation, energy costs, and party strategy.
summary: On Wednesday, Republican Missouri Sen. Josh Hawley called for a nationwide moratorium on data center construction, listing it as a top priority for Senate Republicans to complete over the next six weeks.

Hawley's proposal follows a challenging midterm election where data centers became a focal point of voter outrage, with exit polls showing 76 percent of voters opposed building them in their communities due to concerns over rising utility costs.

Previously, the House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act 417-3, but Senate Democrats blocked the measure in a 57-43 procedural vote on September 30; Hawley and Democratic Connecticut Sen. Richard Blumenthal previously introduced separate power-source legislation.

Across the country, voters passed 40 of 41 ballot measures restricting such projects, including in Texas, where Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa won after campaigning against data center construction, signaling widespread bipartisan concern.

Tech industry leaders are preparing for potential crackdowns in January as more Republicans align with Hawley; while analysts warn that bans could crush economic growth, others suggest firms prioritize facilities outside neighborhoods and farmland.
title: Hawley calls for Senate to pass data center moratorium

bias: Coverage converges on a $63 million FTC -and-17-state settlement over checkout prices exceeding shelf, circular, website, or app prices, but diverges in framing.

Left-Leaning accounts use “deceptive pricing,” “routinely overcharged,” and “every dollar matters,” stressing vulnerable shoppers and detailing $40 million for redress, $20 million for discounts, and $3 million for states.
Center coverage emphasizes eligibility and safeguards preventing repeat discrepancies.
Right-Leaning coverage calls them “pricing complaints,” de-emphasizing pricing mechanics, remedies, and state participation.
The pivotal divide is whether the case signifies recurring consumer harm or a restrained complaint; all perspectives still highlight the settlement and alleged price mismatch.
summary: On Thursday, the Federal Trade Commission and 17 states announced a $63 million settlement with Family Dollar, resolving allegations the retailer persistently overcharged shoppers by charging higher prices at registers than advertised on shelves and mobile apps.

The FTC and states accused Family Dollar of "betraying the trust" of millions, noting the company continued deceptive pricing despite thousands of failed regulatory inspections and numerous consumer complaints across the nation.

Under the settlement, Family Dollar will establish a $40 million restitution fund for eligible customers, provide $20 million in store discounts, and pay $3 million directly to the 17 states that participated in the complaint.
Within 90 days, Family Dollar must implement a pricing accuracy program, train staff to identify discrepancies, and post notices informing customers of their eligibility for settlement benefits.
This agreement follows years of penalties for similar violations; the FTC continues ongoing litigation against the Dollar General Corporation for comparable deceptive pricing practices.
title: Family Dollar reaches $63 million settlement with US FTC, states over customer overcharges

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the inquiry as evidence of possible corruption , spotlighting more than $800 million, alleged “quid pro quo” donor deals, Trump’s “losing his mind” reaction, and labels like “princess of darkness” and “pet projects.” Right-leaning coverage emphasizes Democrats “targeting” Trump’s fundraiser after gaining committee power, presenting the probe as politically motivated while de-emphasizing donor details; its “dark princess” and “corruption investigation” language remains dramatic but ambiguously partisan.

Center coverage uses restrained “probe” and notes “potential corruption.” All perspectives highlight O’Rourke’s role and the investigation, reflecting broader divides over accountability, partisan power, and Trump’s political network.
summary: On Tuesday, Congressional Democrats launched a probe into Meredith O'Rourke, President Donald Trump 's chief fundraiser, over more than $800 million she helped raise for the president's pet projects.
Nicknamed the 'princess of darkness' by Trump, O'Rourke serves as the primary contact for major donors funding the White House ballroom, soliciting gifts ranging from $5 million to $50 million.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, Senator Richard Blumenthal, and Representative Robert Garcia allege the operation 'reeks of potential corruption,' demanding O'Rourke provide detailed records by November 25.

On Thursday, the Justice Department accused Senator Blumenthal of harassment, with U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz threatening 'significant legal consequences' if findings are not secured regarding ballroom donors.
As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January, they plan to utilize subpoena power, though the White House has warned against probes, claiming they constitute crimes.
title: Democrats Open Probe Into Top Trump Fundraiser Meredith O’Rourke

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Trump’s support as politically troubling—“closest allies,” “defend,” and “spy scandal” spotlight unusual access and the unresolved possibility that sensitive technology reached China.

Right-Leaning coverage portrays the intervention as loyalty to an “AI king” and protection of a vital American company, while invoking “China spy scandal,” “secretly,” and “suspicions spread” to stress espionage and semiconductor security.
Center coverage more cautiously emphasizes the reported “fight” for Huang’s job, succession uncertainty, and interim leadership.
The dividing line is whether Trump’s call signals questionable favoritism or economic stewardship; all perspectives highlight Huang’s resignation, family distress, and Nvidia’s consequential future.
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down following scrutiny over his personal life, with Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress assuming interim leadership while the board searches for a permanent successor.

The board launched an investigation Sunday into Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a businesswoman US authorities suspect of spying for China; Nvidia has lost about US$300 billion in market value since.
President Donald Trump called Huang on Tuesday, urging the executive to fight for his job, and previously stated he had "done an amazing job for our country," the New York Times reported.
Kress stated the company will "continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing," as Huang's departure creates uncertainty for the AI ecosystem he helped bankroll.
Nvidia is scheduled to present third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on November 17, a key test as the company navigates the leadership transition and US chip export policy uncertainties.
title: Trump had urged Jensen Huang to fight for his job: report

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the infant’s death as evidence of a broader humanitarian crisis, using phrases like “continues to block aid,” “serious risk,” and “dramatic conditions,” while citing eleven prior hypothermia deaths and warnings affecting more than half a million children .
Center coverage focuses on the reported hypothermia death in a tent, the father, and the doctor, with “growing fears” but limited blame.
Right-Leaning accounts emphasize “worsening winter conditions,” the father “in shock,” and sometimes label Civil Defense “run by Hamas,” shifting attention toward source context.

All perspectives highlight the nine-month-old’s death, displacement, cold, and Gaza’s vulnerable civilians, reflecting wider disputes over Israeli responsibility, humanitarian access, and Hamas’s role.
summary: Nine-Month-Old Kinan Ahmad Raqiq died from hypothermia inside his family's displacement tent in Khan Yunis, a doctor told AFP after days of harsh weather and flooding in the Gaza Strip.

Heavy rain last week flooded tens of thousands of tents in Gaza, where the UN's Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reported 26,000 households were affected and around 65 percent of the population remains displaced.
James Elder, spokesman on Gaza for UNICEF, warned that flooding marks only the beginning of the cold season, stating, "It's very important to know how bad things are in Gaza. It's not yet winter."

In a Wednesday response to the Board of Peace, Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel provided 91,000 tents, asserting, "Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza."
Five people including three children died when a sandy embankment collapsed onto their tents the day after the flooding, compounding the humanitarian crisis across the territory.
title: Nine-Month-Old Baby Dies of Cold in Gaza

bias: Coverage divides over scope and emphasis: the left-leaning framing foregrounds “high alert” and the mission to “thwart terror,” presenting the Jordan border visit primarily as counterterrorism, while right-leaning accounts expand it into a doctrine of “constant readiness,” warning of “rapid changes and surprise” across all fronts.
The right also portrays the Jordan Valley as an “eastern defensive wall” and highlights the 96th Gilad Regional Division—context de-emphasized by the left.
No center perspective is provided.
Both sides emphasize Eyal Zamir’s border tour and military preparedness, reflecting a broader divide between narrowly framed threat prevention and expansive security-first vigilance.
summary: On Wednesday, Gen. Eyal Zamir visited the eastern border with Jordan to inspect military posts and a barrier under construction, emphasizing readiness against potential threats.
Zamir toured a sector assigned to the 96th Gilad Regional Division, which monitors the frontier stretching from the Israel-Jordan-Syria tri-border area southward past the Dead Sea.
Calling the Jordan Valley 'Israel's eastern defensive wall,' Zamir described the area as an 'essential component of our national security and strategic depth' amid IDF reinforcements.
The military chief stated forces must be prepared for 'rapid change and surprise,' as the division applies lessons from the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack to address infiltration threats.
Accompanied by senior officers including Central Command head Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, Zamir met with leaders of the Jordan Valley Regional Council to strengthen regional security cooperation.
title: IDF Chief Stresses Need for Constant Readiness During Jordan Border Visit

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the case as “arbitrary detention,” saying Israel “refuses” release and is “neglecting” Abu Safiyah’s “deteriorating health,” while emphasizing weight loss, abnormal blood tests, the “unlawful combatants law,” and Gaza’s “severe shortage” of medical personnel.

The right-leaning presentation is narrower and more procedural, foregrounding the court ’s refusal to release 14 doctors and describing “health concerns” without broader allegations or medical detail.

summary: Israeli courts rejected petitions seeking the release of 14 Palestinian doctors from Gaza who are held without charges or trials.
The Lod District Court refused Dr. Hussam Abu Safia’s request for an independent medical examination and a second medical opinion.
Physicians for Human Rights Israel said Abu Safia had lost 14 kilograms, experienced falling hemoglobin levels, and had chest pain that was not properly investigated.
The group said the detentions further weaken Gaza’s healthcare system, which faces a severe shortage of medical workers after widespread infrastructure damage.
title: Israeli Court Refuses to Release 14 Gaza Doctors Held without Charge or Trial

Right-Leaning coverage largely shares the loss-centered framing but emphasizes voters sending a “message,” gas prices, and lawmakers forced to “clear out their offices,” rather than defending the party.
Center coverage is more restrained, presenting “unexpected losses,” Democratic control of Congress, and internal reassessment.

The pivotal divide is whether defeat reflects Republican confusion or voter rebuke; all perspectives agree on losses, closed-door meetings, Hudson’s role, and gas-price dissatisfaction, reflecting broader disputes over accountability and political momentum.
summary: Back on Capitol Hill this week, House Speaker Mike Johnson said voters made the "wrong choice" as Democrats flipped more than 40 Republican-held seats, positioning them for their most robust majority since the early years of Barack Obama's presidency.

Rep. Richard Hudson noted voters were sending a message as frustration grew among Republicans who felt they lost touch with voters after being awarded full control of the White House and Congress two years earlier.

House Republicans elected Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan as their next leader, reflecting a fighting stance. Jordan, a co-founder of the House Freedom Caucus who chairs the Judiciary Committee, has waged heated fights against Democrats and remains a top ally of President Donald Trump.

In the Senate, Republicans re-elected Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota without a voice vote after hours of deliberation. Sen. Bernie Moreno said the party decided to "let our leader be the leader," despite some conservatives arguing for a delay.

Republicans are weighing how to proceed, balancing calls for moderation against hard-line positions that might reenergize the base. They are scrutinizing the calendar to push through their remaining agenda before Democrats assume control of the House and the Senate in January.
title: Republicans Dazed by Midterm Election Defeats Grapple with What Went Wrong

bias: Left-Leaning coverage casts Nick Shirley’s retraction as a political and moral collapse, using phrases such as “ MAGA darling,” “humiliated,” “embarrassing,” and “fraud smear,” while stressing angry calls targeting Lam’s Seafood and sympathy for the family-run Asian store.

Center and right perspectives de-emphasize partisan identity and instead frame the episode narrowly as Shirley “retracts” or “corrected” claims about “alleged” EBT fraud, with the right avoiding broader accusations about motive or misconduct; center coverage adds transaction-specific context.

summary: On Wednesday, social media influencer Nick Shirley retracted his October allegations that Lam's Seafood Asian Market in Seattle facilitated EBT fraud, admitting his claims about a $120 transaction were incorrect.
Shirley previously claimed a customer bought a single can of Spam and sushi for $120, but Lam's clarified the customer actually purchased a full case of 24 cans of Spam.
After the video racked up nearly 600,000 views, operations manager Teizi Mersai reported that Lam's faced significant backlash, including abusive phone calls and lost customers.
Shirley pulled the videos 30 days after Lam's hired an attorney and sent a cease and desist letter, leveraging Washington defamation law which allows time to issue corrections and mitigate claims.

A 24-year-old influencer with roughly 2 million YouTube subscribers, Shirley previously rose to prominence targeting Somali-run daycare centers in Minnesota, though none were found to have committed fraud.
title: Influencer Nick Shirley Retracts Food Stamp Fraud Allegations Against Seattle Supermarket
